description: Meet the wild cats of the world, from lions and tigers to the tiny rusty-spotted cat, in a short children's book written by Wikijunior volunteers for ages 8–12. Each day you read one page together, then build a homemade field guide with a card for every cat, find its home on a map, and talk about how people can help cats survive. It's a free, openly licensed book; every page is free to read on Wikibooks.
includes: Link to the free Wikibooks page for every lesson
A homemade cat field guide, one card per species
Map work for each cat's home range
Questions with answers for every lesson

units.title: Unit 1: Meet the Cats and the Roaring Cats

lessons.title: Lesson 1: A Note to Parents and Meet the Cats
steps: Parent: read the short foreword
Read Meet the Cats together
Start a field guide: a folder or notebook with one page per cat
questions: Which cat rules Africa, and which rules Asia?
On which two continents are there no native wild cats?
answers: The lion rules Africa; the tiger rules Asia

lessons.title: Lesson 2: The Lion
steps: Read the page together
Add a cat card to your field guide: where it lives, what it looks like, what it eats
On a map, find the savannas of Africa and the Gir forest of India
questions: What is a group of lions called?
Who does most of the hunting in a pride?
Do lions really live in the jungle?
answers: No, they live on grassy savannas

lessons.title: Lesson 3: The Tiger
steps: Read the page together
Add a cat card to your field guide: where it lives, what it looks like, what it eats
Draw a tiger and give it your own stripe pattern
questions: What is the largest cat living today?
Do any two tigers have the same stripes?
Why might people near tigers wear a mask on the back of the head?
answers: Tigers like to attack from behind

lessons.title: Lesson 4: The Leopard
steps: Read the page together
Add a cat card to your field guide: where it lives, what it looks like, what it eats
Narrate why leopards drag their food up into trees
questions: Which big cat lives in more places than any other?
What two Greek words make up the name 'leopard'?

lessons.title: Lesson 5: The Jaguar
steps: Read the page together
Add a cat card to your field guide: where it lives, what it looks like, what it eats
Compare a jaguar and a leopard picture side by side
questions: What is the largest cat in the Americas (the New World)?
Where do jaguars like to live?
answers: Rain forests, by rivers and swamps, in South and Central America

units.title: Unit 2: Mountain, Forest and Speedy Cats

lessons.title: Lesson 6: The Snow Leopard
steps: Read the page together
Add a cat card to your field guide: where it lives, what it looks like, what it eats
Find the Himalayas on a map
questions: In which mountains do many snow leopards live?
How does a snow leopard's fur help it hide?
answers: Its gray and black swirls match the rocks

lessons.title: Lesson 7: The Clouded Leopard and the Marbled Cat
steps: Read both pages
Make a card for each cat
Narrate how these two cats are alike
questions: Is the clouded leopard a true leopard?
How big is the marbled cat?
answers: Only a little bigger than a pet cat

lessons.title: Lesson 8: The Cheetah
steps: Read the page together
Add a cat card to your field guide: where it lives, what it looks like, what it eats
Measure 100 meters outdoors and talk about how fast a cheetah covers it
questions: What is the fastest land animal?
About how fast can a cheetah run?

lessons.title: Lesson 9: The Puma
steps: Read the page together
Add a cat card to your field guide: where it lives, what it looks like, what it eats
Act out what to do if you meet a puma: stand tall, don't run
questions: What are some other names for the puma?
Can a puma roar?
Should you run if you see a puma?
answers: No; stand tall and face it

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Lynx and Bobcats
steps: Read the page together
Add a cat card to your field guide: where it lives, what it looks like, what it eats
Find Spain on a map: home of the endangered Iberian lynx
questions: What job do lynx do especially well?
Which is the smallest kind of lynx?
answers: Keeping the rabbit population under control

units.title: Unit 3: Smaller Wild Cats and Hybrids

lessons.title: Lesson 11: The Ocelot and the Margay
steps: Read both pages
Make a card for each cat
Narrate how the margay gets around in the trees
questions: What once brought ocelots close to extinction?
How can a margay nap in a tree?
answers: People hunting them for their beautiful fur
Hanging upside down by its back feet

lessons.title: Lesson 12: The Jaguarundi and the Rusty-Spotted Cat
steps: Read both pages
Make a card for each cat
Find India and Sri Lanka on a map
questions: What animal is a jaguarundi often mistaken for?
What is the smallest member of the cat family?

lessons.title: Lesson 13: The Caracal and the Serval
steps: Read both pages
Make a card for each cat
Jump straight up and see how high you go; a serval leaps to catch birds
questions: What does the name 'caracal' mean?
Where do servals live?

lessons.title: Lesson 14: The Manul, the Wild Cat and the Sand Cat
steps: Read the three short pages
Make a card for each cat
Narrate how the sand cat's furry feet help it in the desert
questions: Which wild cat is the ancestor of our pet cats?
Which is the oldest living species of cat?

lessons.title: Lesson 15: Tigons, Ligers and Other Hybrids
steps: Read the four short pages
Draw a chart: which parents make a liger, a tigon, a pumapard
Talk about the marozi: what is a cryptid, and how do we know what's real?
questions: What are a liger's parents?
What is a cryptid?
answers: A lion father and a tiger mother
An animal known only from stories, not studied by scientists
lessons.notes: The Marozi page is mostly about a legend; treat it as a lesson in telling stories from science.

units.title: Unit 4: How Cats Live, Then and Now

lessons.title: Lesson 16: Raising Young
steps: Read the page together
Watch a pet cat or a video of kittens playing, and spot hunting moves
Narrate how play helps cubs

links.label: Read: How do cats raise their young?

questions: What are young big cats called?
About when do cubs open their eyes?

lessons.title: Lesson 17: Fossil History
steps: Read the page together
Draw a sabre-toothed Smilodon
Narrate one fossil cat you'd like to have seen
questions: What was the small animal that all carnivores came from?
What was the largest cat that ever lived?

lessons.title: Lesson 18: In Danger of Extinction
steps: Read the page together
List the dangers big cats face
Talk about one thing your family could do to help
questions: What does the book call 'the silent killer' of big cats?
What do we call people who break the law to kill animals?

lessons.title: Lesson 19: Keeping Cats in Zoos
steps: Read the page together
Visit a zoo or a zoo website and look for enrichment toys
Narrate how keepers keep big cats healthy and happy
questions: How many types of fitness does the zoo keeper describe?
Why do zoos run Species Survival Plans?
answers: To help endangered cats breed and stay healthy

lessons.title: Lesson 20: Cat Classification and Review
steps: Read the classification page together
Sort your field guide cards into groups by genus
Look up any new words in the Glossary
questions: What family do all cats belong to?
Why do scientists give each animal one Latin name?
answers: So people speaking different languages don't get confused
